vignette_text: You have one free evening this week. A friend you have not seen for a while invites you over. You had planned to finish a project you enjoy. Either plan would take the whole evening. Your friend understands if you cannot come. The project has no deadline.
appraisal_text: I should spend the evening with my friend.

vignette_text: Your club has money left for one activity. A nearby trip would give members something new to try. Buying games would give the club more to do at its weekly meetings. The two plans cost the same. Members like both ideas, but the club can only fund one.
appraisal_text: I should vote to spend the money on the trip.

vignette_text: You can choose between two weekend jobs. One is at a shop where you know the staff and the work. The other pays more and would teach you new skills. It starts much earlier in the morning. Both jobs offer the same number of hours, and you cannot take both.
appraisal_text: I should take the job at the familiar shop.

vignette_text: You can join one of two classes that meet at the same time. Both teach the same skills. The nearby class costs more. The class across town costs less but adds an hour of travel each week. You can afford either, but can sign up for only one.
appraisal_text: I should pay more for the nearby class.

vignette_text: Your group report is due tomorrow. One part needs work. Its writer can fix it tonight, but has missed deadlines before. You could do it, using your free evening. Only one person can edit the final file tonight. The group asks you to choose who will handle it.
appraisal_text: I should rewrite that part myself.

vignette_text: A friend asks to borrow your camera for a day trip. You do not need it that day. They have been careful with things they borrowed before, but this camera would be hard for you to replace. Their phone takes photos, though not as well as your camera.
appraisal_text: I should lend my friend the camera.

vignette_text: You spot a small mistake in a teammate’s slides. You can fix it now, or leave it for them tomorrow. Either way, it will be ready before the talk. Your team usually lets each person edit their own work. You must choose who will make this change.
appraisal_text: I should fix the mistake myself.

vignette_text: A close friend invites you to celebrate in another town. You can pay for the trip, but it would use the money you saved for something you wanted. Your friend would love to see you and understands the cost. You could celebrate together at home another day.
appraisal_text: I should use my saved money to make the trip.

vignette_text: A friend asks you to check a poster before it goes to print tonight. You like the design, but some words are hard to read. They can still make one change. You must either approve this version or return it for changes. You can include a kind note with either.
appraisal_text: I should return the poster for changes.

vignette_text: You are choosing a place for a short trip with a friend. One room is small but close to the places you want to visit. The other is larger and quieter, but each outing needs a bus ride. Both cost the same. Your friend is happy with either.
appraisal_text: I should choose the smaller room near the sights.

vignette_text: Your club asks you to lead its next event. You want to try leading, and someone can help you learn. The role would take extra time during a busy month. You could instead keep a smaller role you know well. Another member is willing to lead if you do not.
appraisal_text: I should take the lead role for this event.

vignette_text: You have started a story and feel excited about it. A friend offers to read the first draft. Their feedback has helped you before, but hearing suggestions early can make it harder to follow your own ideas. You can share it now or wait until the draft is finished.
appraisal_text: I should share the unfinished draft with my friend.

vignette_text: You have planned a day out with a friend. Someone at your weekend job asks you to cover their shift that day. The team would be short of help if you say no, but the manager says it is your choice. Your friend has been looking forward to the outing.
appraisal_text: I should cover the shift and cancel the outing.

vignette_text: Your group must choose one theme for an event today. Most members favor a familiar theme that is easy to plan. You prefer a new theme that could draw more people but needs more work. There is time for either plan. Each member gets one vote between the two.
appraisal_text: I should vote for the new theme.

vignette_text: Your bike needs a repair. The shop says it should work well afterward. You can spend your travel money on the repair or a bus pass for this month, but not both. The bus reaches the same places. Its times do not always fit your plans.
appraisal_text: I should spend my travel money on the bike repair.

vignette_text: You signed up for a day trip with a friend, but they can no longer go. You still want to visit the place. You know a few other people on the trip, though not well. You can get your money back if you cancel today.
appraisal_text: I should go on the trip without my friend.

vignette_text: A relative asks you to help them move on Saturday. Helping means joining the van for the whole day; a short visit will not work. You had planned to rest after a busy week. They have enough helpers, but another person would make the work easier.
appraisal_text: I should spend Saturday helping my relative move.

vignette_text: You have one free hour for exercise each week. A friend invites you to a class at that time. The fee fits your budget, but leaves less for treats. Your other option is a free outdoor group that meets at the same time. You do not know anyone there.
appraisal_text: I should join the paid class with my friend.

vignette_text: In a meeting, a teammate shares an idea you made together without naming your part. You can add your name while the group discusses it, or stay quiet now and talk privately later. You do not know why they left you out. The choice is whether to speak up now.
appraisal_text: I should mention my part during the meeting.

vignette_text: You have promised to finish a personal project for a local show. To finish in time, you would need to work on it most evenings this week. You had hoped for a quieter week. You can skip this show and enter the next one in two months.
appraisal_text: I should work this week to enter the coming show.

vignette_text: A place opens in a class you have wanted to take. It starts next week, which is already busy for you. You can make time, but would have to drop some plans. The same class may run again later in the year, though no date is set.
appraisal_text: I should take the open place in next week's class.

vignette_text: You need to book one room for an hour of work. The shared room has a large desk and quiet music that will stay on. The smaller room is silent but has less desk space. Once your hour starts, you cannot switch rooms. Both are free.
appraisal_text: I should book the shared room with the larger desk.

vignette_text: Your group is making a short video. You can take a role you already do well, or try one you have wanted to learn. The new role would be harder and might slow the group at first. Another member can take either role and will help you learn.
appraisal_text: I should take the role I already know well.

vignette_text: A friend plans a birthday meal that costs more than you usually spend. You can afford it by using this month’s meal budget. You could instead meet them for a cheaper meal later and keep some money. You can budget for one meal, and your friend welcomes either plan.
appraisal_text: I should join the group for the birthday meal.

vignette_text: A morning train starts leaving 25 minutes later. Over the next few months, more people ride it. Road work also begins on a nearby highway, making car trips slower. The train fare stays the same. The train company has not asked new riders why they changed their travel plans.
appraisal_text: The later start time helped bring more riders to the train.

vignette_text: An online shop starts charging a small fee to return items. Fewer items are sent back, while sales stay about the same. Some shoppers say they now check sizes more carefully. Others say they keep things they do not like because returning them is no longer worth the cost.
appraisal_text: More careful choices before buying helped reduce the number of returns.

vignette_text: A school stops giving letter grades in one science class and uses pass or fail instead. More students then choose the next science class. Test scores stay about the same. The school also starts a science club that year. Students have not been asked why they chose the next class.
appraisal_text: The new grading system helped make more students want to keep studying science.

vignette_text: A library stops charging fees for late books. More overdue books come back over the next year. The library also starts sending text reminders when books are due. Some people return books that have been missing for months. Staff do not know which change mattered most to the people returning books.
appraisal_text: Ending late fees helped bring more overdue books back.

vignette_text: A snack company changes to bags that use less plastic. More customers buy its snacks again in the next few months. The snacks and prices stay the same. Reviews often praise the new bags, but most buyers leave no review. The company has not tracked other reasons people buy again.
appraisal_text: The new bags helped bring customers back to buy the snacks again.

vignette_text: A team stops holding meetings on Wednesdays. People say they get more work done alone that day. However, shared tasks take longer to finish. Some workers say they now wait until Thursday to get answers from teammates. Others still get quick answers through messages. The team is the same size.
appraisal_text: Waiting longer for answers helped cause the slowdown in shared tasks.

vignette_text: A town puts brighter lights on several shopping streets. Fewer thefts are reported there at night over the next year. More police also begin visiting those streets. Nearby streets without new lights show a smaller drop in reported thefts. The town does not know how many thefts went unreported.
appraisal_text: The brighter lights helped reduce thefts on the shopping streets.

vignette_text: A cafeteria adds several meals made without meat. It sells more lunches, with no change in prices. Some customers praise the new food, and some say the lines now move faster. The cafeteria counts total sales but does not record which change brought in people who did not eat there before.
appraisal_text: Liking the new food helped bring more people to the cafeteria.

vignette_text: An app changes its background from blue to green. More users open it each day during the next week. No tools or buttons change. A few users praise the new look, while others dislike it. There is no comparison group, and the team has only checked the first week.
appraisal_text: The new color helped bring users back to the app that week.

vignette_text: A team switches from five workdays to four, keeping the same pay. It finishes about the same amount of work each month. Meetings become shorter, and some workers say they focus better. Others say they sometimes finish tasks at home on their day off. Those extra hours are not recorded.
appraisal_text: Better use of time helped the team finish the same work in four days.

vignette_text: A cafe stops taking tips and raises workers' hourly pay. More workers leave over the next few months. Some had earned more when tips were included. Others now earn more than before. A nearby cafe is also hiring. The owner has not asked the workers why they left.
appraisal_text: Lower total earnings helped cause more workers to leave the cafe.

vignette_text: A team begins working in the office three days a week after working from home. More staff leave that year. People with long trips to work leave more often than those living nearby. The team also gets a new manager. Staff have not been asked why they chose to leave.
appraisal_text: The trip to the office helped cause more staff to leave.

vignette_text: You want to understand how online ratings work. Two games both have four stars. One has twenty reviews; the other has two thousand. The reviews come from people who chose to post. You wonder how much the number of reviews tells you about how well the rating matches players’ views.
appraisal_text: The game with more reviews has a rating that better reflects its players’ views.

vignette_text: You are learning how polls describe a group. A school asks students in its art club which new clubs they want. Most choose another arts club. All grades are included, but only art club members answer. You want to understand how well these answers describe the whole school.
appraisal_text: This poll gives a useful picture of what clubs the whole school wants.

vignette_text: You want to understand how an app picks videos for your feed. You watch several cooking clips, and your feed has many more afterward. The app gives no details about its choices. You also follow two cooks. You wonder what your feed can tell you about your interests.
appraisal_text: My video feed gives a good picture of the full range of things I enjoy.

vignette_text: You want to understand why maps of the same park look different. One shows paths, hills, and streams. Another shows bus stops, entrances, and buildings. Both were updated this year. You are learning what makes a map useful, even when it leaves out details shown on another map.
appraisal_text: The map with more details is the more useful guide to the park.

vignette_text: You are learning what an average can tell you. Two help desks both report an average wait of ten minutes. At one, most people wait about ten minutes. At the other, some get help right away while others wait much longer. You wonder how similar the service really is.
appraisal_text: The two desks offer a similar waiting experience because their average waits match.

vignette_text: You want to understand what it means to learn a skill well. In a typing lesson, one learner is fast but makes mistakes. Another is slower but rarely makes an error. Both have had the same practice time. You wonder how speed and accuracy fit together when judging progress.
appraisal_text: The faster learner has made more progress at typing.

vignette_text: You want to understand the difference between knowing facts and using them. A learner can repeat all the steps from a lesson but needs help with a new problem. Another forgets some names but solves it alone. You wonder what each kind of performance shows about understanding.
appraisal_text: Solving the new problem shows a deeper understanding than repeating the steps.

vignette_text: You want to understand how to judge a chatbot’s answer. It gives a clear explanation about an old building and names two sources. One source discusses the building, but you cannot find the other. You do not yet know which details are correct or how the answer was made.
appraisal_text: This answer is a useful starting point for learning about the building.

vignette_text: You are learning how to compare two ways of studying. One class uses flashcards and another uses practice questions. The second class scores higher, but it also had higher scores before the study began. Both classes cover the same topic. You wonder how much this comparison tells you.
appraisal_text: This comparison gives useful evidence that practice questions work better than flashcards.

vignette_text: You want to understand how a headline can shape a story. A headline says a park is losing visitors. The article says visits fell during a rainy month but rose over the whole year. You wonder whether the headline gives readers a fair picture of what happened.
appraisal_text: The headline gives a fair summary of the park’s visitor numbers.

vignette_text: You are learning why people use small models of real places. A model of a town shows roads and buildings but leaves out traffic and people. It helps explain where things are. You wonder whether leaving out so much makes it a poor way to learn about the town.
appraisal_text: The model is still a useful way to understand the town.

vignette_text: You want to understand how people judge whether a game is successful. One game has many players who leave after a week. Another has fewer players who keep playing for months. Both earn the same amount. You wonder which numbers best show how well a game is doing.
appraisal_text: The game with more players should be seen as more successful.

vignette_text: You finish a course you worked hard on for months. You still like the skill you learned. During the course, you worked with other people each week. Now the final project is done, and the weekly meetings have ended.
appraisal_text: Working toward the goal mattered more to me than finishing it.

vignette_text: For years, you have handled the plans for a group. Now another person takes a turn. Their way works, though it differs from yours. You have less to do, and questions that used to come to you now go to them.
appraisal_text: Being needed was an important part of why I liked that role.

vignette_text: You have painted for years. Lately, you spend more time choosing what to post online than trying new ideas. You still paint some days without sharing the results.
appraisal_text: Trying to impress other people has taken some joy out of painting.

vignette_text: Friends help you finish a task after you fall behind. You had planned to do it alone. You have helped them with similar tasks before. No one complains about lending a hand, and the task gets done on time.
appraisal_text: I hold myself to a stricter rule about needing help than I hold my friends to.

vignette_text: You leave a day free after several busy weeks. Each time you sit down, you get up again to do another small task. By evening, you have done many things and spent little time resting. Nothing had to be finished that day.
appraisal_text: I link having a good day too closely with getting things done.

vignette_text: After a tiring day, you speak sharply to someone who asks a simple question. They stay calm, and you later apologize. They accept it. You usually try to be patient with people, including when you have had a hard day.
appraisal_text: That reply reflects a hard day more than the kind of person I am.

vignette_text: You visit a place where you spent time when you were younger. Much has changed. Some familiar places are still there, but you no longer see the same people there. Your life now has things you value too.
appraisal_text: I miss that time in my life more than I miss the place itself.

vignette_text: You used to fill each weekend with group plans. Lately, you have been leaving more time free to spend on your own. You still like your friends and see them regularly. Nothing has gone wrong between you.
appraisal_text: My wish for quiet time reflects a change in what I value.

vignette_text: Two people praise something you made. One knows the work well and mentions details. The other is someone you have wanted to impress and gives a brief compliment. You hear both comments on the same day.
appraisal_text: Whose praise I receive matters to me more than how useful it is.

vignette_text: Your group repeats an old yearly tradition. The same people meet for the same activity. You still make time to go, though you rarely choose that activity on your own anymore. Others seem open to trying something new next year.
appraisal_text: What I value is the shared history more than the activity itself.

vignette_text: A friend often turns to you when things go wrong. You care about them and often spend a long time listening. They listen when you ask to change the topic. You usually wait until late in the call to bring up your own news.
appraisal_text: I worry that setting limits would make me a less caring friend.

vignette_text: You begin a hobby where you are a beginner again. You need help with simple steps and sometimes have to start over. Most of your other hobbies are things you already do well. You keep attending the weekly sessions.
appraisal_text: Feeling capable matters to me more than I had realized.

vignette_text: You started practicing for a contest because you wanted to win. After months of practice, the weekly sessions are part of your routine. You have met people there and learned new skills. You still plan to enter the contest.
appraisal_text: My reasons for doing this have grown rather than my goal becoming less important.

vignette_text: You agree to a small favor before checking your own plans. Later, you realize it will make your day rushed. The person had said it was fine if you could not help. You have agreed to favors before checking your plans several times lately.
appraisal_text: Avoiding someone’s disappointment matters too much when I agree to favors.

vignette_text: You find drawings you made years ago. Some show ideas you still use; others have mistakes you would now know how to fix. You have kept both the old drawings and your recent work.
appraisal_text: I judge my past work too much by what I can do now.

vignette_text: You join a group where people share different interests from your old friends. You try new things with them. You talk more about some topics with one group and other topics with the other. You continue spending time with both groups.
appraisal_text: Acting differently in these groups still fits with being myself.

vignette_text: A plan is canceled, leaving you with a free afternoon. You choose what to do as the day goes on, instead of making another schedule. You usually plan your days closely. By evening, you have done several things you had not planned to do.
appraisal_text: Knowing what to expect matters to me as much as the plan itself.

vignette_text: You and a friend both finish projects you care about. At a gathering, people ask your friend about their work and praise it. No one knows much about your work yet. You had hoped to tell the group about it too.
appraisal_text: Wanting recognition for myself can fit with being happy for my friend.

vignette_text: You try a new way to spend your evening and decide you would like to do it again. Still, the next day you return to your usual routine. Both activities are available, and either would fit the time you have.
appraisal_text: Familiarity guides my free time more than enjoyment does.

vignette_text: You complete a difficult puzzle alone. Later, you solve another with friends, and they find several answers. Both puzzles take effort and are about equally hard. You finish one using only your own answers and the other by sharing the work.
appraisal_text: Doing it on my own adds something important to my sense of success.

vignette_text: Friends often call you the quiet one. You used to agree, but lately you speak up more in new groups. With old friends, you still tend to listen. They continue using the same label when they introduce you to someone.
appraisal_text: The old label influences how I act around these friends.

vignette_text: You change your view after hearing a thoughtful explanation. You had stated your earlier view clearly to the same people. No one makes fun of you or asks you to defend the old view. The new explanation answers a question you had not considered before.
appraisal_text: Being seen as consistent matters too much to me in these moments.

vignette_text: You finish a small task you had put off for weeks. It takes little time. Yesterday, you finished a much larger task that you had started right away. Both tasks were useful, and neither brought any special praise.
appraisal_text: The relief of finally doing it explains more of my satisfaction than the result.

vignette_text: You sort through old things and keep a worn ticket from a day with friends. You throw away newer things that cost more. The ticket has no use now. You put it back with the things you plan to keep.
appraisal_text: What the ticket represents matters more to me than the object itself.

vignette_text: You spend several evenings helping plan a group event. Afterward, the organizer sends a message thanking several people by name but leaves you out. They thanked you in person before you left the event.
appraisal_text: The group valued my help less than other people’s help.

vignette_text: You train for several months to run a long race. Near the end, your legs start to cramp. You finish, but take longer than your goal time. Your family cheers for you at the finish line.
appraisal_text: Missing my goal shows that my training did not prepare me well enough.

vignette_text: During a group meeting, you say that the recent deadlines have been hard to manage. Two people nod, but the group leader moves to the next topic without a reply. The meeting continues without returning to your concern.
appraisal_text: The group leader did not take my concern seriously.

vignette_text: You share a project draft with someone who has helped you learn for two years. They suggest many changes and say the main idea needs more work. They also say they are glad you tried something new.
appraisal_text: The feedback shows that I am not yet ready to do this kind of work on my own.

vignette_text: You see a photo of three work friends having lunch together nearby. No one asked you to join them. You had chatted with them that morning, and nothing seemed different. You do not know when they made the plan.
appraisal_text: I am less included in this group than I thought.

vignette_text: At a family meal, a relative makes a brief joke about how you dress. They then turn to someone else and start a new conversation. This relative has made similar comments before. Other people keep talking as usual.
appraisal_text: This relative does not respect how I choose to dress.

vignette_text: You and someone close to you usually mark a special date by spending time together. This year, they forget until you mention it the next day. They apologize and say the week has been busy.
appraisal_text: The busy week is the main reason they forgot our special date.

vignette_text: A friend used to turn down your ideas for weekend trips, saying they did not enjoy traveling. You now hear they have taken two trips with new friends. You have not talked about what changed.
appraisal_text: My friend used travel as an excuse to turn down plans with me.

vignette_text: You give a talk that you spent weeks preparing. Afterward, someone you know says, “That was much better than I expected.” They smile, and others say the talk went well.
appraisal_text: The comment shows that this person had a low opinion of my skills.

vignette_text: A relative quickly helps your sibling with a hard task. You recently handled a similar task alone without asking for help, even though it was difficult. The relative did not offer to help you with yours.
appraisal_text: My relative assumes I need less help than my sibling.

vignette_text: You join a project team and have been doing well for several months. You later learn that someone else was offered your place first but turned it down. The team has given you good feedback since you joined.
appraisal_text: My work so far shows that I belong on this team.

vignette_text: You share a creative project online after working on it for months. Most comments are kind, but one person gives a long, harsh review. That review points out specific problems. Other people describe parts of the project that they enjoyed.
appraisal_text: The harsh review deserves more weight than the positive comments.

vignette_text: You have set aside an evening for a friend’s visit, planned a week ago. On the day, they cancel because they are worn out. They say they want to pick another date but have not named one.
appraisal_text: Seeing me matters less to my friend than I thought.

vignette_text: You try a new group activity and struggle with the basic steps. Other people seem to pick them up quickly. The leader says beginners often need time and invites you back.
appraisal_text: I struggled more than the group expected a beginner to struggle.

vignette_text: A mug someone made for you breaks when you knock it off a shelf. It cannot be fixed. You still have photos and other gifts from them. The space where you kept the mug is now empty.
appraisal_text: The mug held a part of our connection that other keepsakes cannot replace.

vignette_text: You sign up for a small workshop and set aside the day to attend. Later, the organizer says it is full and returns your fee. They made a mistake with the number of places. They apologize and offer you the next date, months away.
appraisal_text: The organizer did not give my plans enough care.

vignette_text: You tell a funny story in a group chat, but no one replies. Messages soon turn to another topic. You had chatted with everyone earlier that day. You do not know whether people saw the whole story.
appraisal_text: The group thought my story was awkward.

vignette_text: You finish your first day helping at a local event. You needed several reminders. The other helpers were kind, but seemed much faster. The organizer thanks you and asks you to return next week.
appraisal_text: My help today created more work than it saved.

vignette_text: You arrive for a group outing and learn the plan has changed. The new place is harder for you to reach, so you go home. The others apologize and say the change happened quickly. No one checked with you before they left.
appraisal_text: The group gave too little thought to whether I could join.

vignette_text: You make a mistake near the end of a close team game. Your team loses. Several other chances were missed earlier, and teammates say the result was not on one person.
appraisal_text: My mistake deserves most of the blame for the loss.

vignette_text: You tell a friend you have had a rough day and ask to talk. They say they will call, but do not. The next morning they apologize and explain that they fell asleep. They have listened to you before.
appraisal_text: I cannot count on this friend when I need support.

vignette_text: At a small show, your work is displayed with someone else’s name. A staff member fixes it as soon as you ask, but some guests have already left. You worked hard to have something ready for the show.
appraisal_text: The mix-up took away a meaningful part of being in the show.

vignette_text: A friend is moving away. You planned to spend an afternoon together, but packing runs late and you only get a short goodbye. They hug you and promise to stay in touch.
appraisal_text: The short goodbye means our friendship is already becoming less close.

vignette_text: You put effort into an entry for a small art show, but it is not chosen. The note says there were many more entries than spaces. A friend tells you they liked your piece.
appraisal_text: Not being chosen means this piece needs much more work.
